interest: This document provides evidence of German-Japanese cultural diplomacy in the period leading up to the Anti-Comintern Pact of November 1936, highlighting the Japanese government's official sponsorship of prominent German cultural figures such as the pianist Professor Wilhelm Kempff. It also illustrates how the U.S. State Department tracked international cultural exchanges and foreign influence across Asia through its network of consular posts.
overview: This file (894.42762 / File 612) consists of a Department of State List of Papers sheet cataloguing records on cultural and educational relations between Japan and Germany. It records despatch No. 538 from the American consulate in Singapore, dated June 18, 1936, prepared by McEnelly, which reported on an officially sponsored concert tour of Japan by the renowned German pianist Professor Wilhelm Kempff.

subfiles.about: Department of State list of papers recording a despatch from Singapore concerning a government-sponsored tour of Japan by German pianist Professor Wilhelm Kempff.
subfiles.summary: This document is a Department of State List of Papers indexing document No. 1 filed under decimal classification 894.42762. It logs despatch No. 538 from Singapore, dated June 18, 1936, by consular officer McEnelly. The entry provides an abstract indicating that the despatch reported on a tour of Japan by German pianist Professor Wilhelm Kempff sponsored by the Japanese government.
